items.title: Project Red Zone: Undercover Operation Seizes 23 Firearms, Including One Linked to Mississauga Homicide
items.summary: Region of Peel – Peel Regional Police’s Specialized Enforcement Bureau, in collaboration with the United States Department of Homeland Security and Criminal Intelligence Service Ontario (CISO), successfully infiltrated and disrupted a firearm trafficking network operating across the Greater Toronto Area (GTA). 75 grams of cocaine, and more than 950 rounds of ammunition. One of the firearms recovered through Project Red Zone has been linked to a March 2024 homicide in Mississauga, in which one male was fatally shot and another sustained serious injuries. The investigation determined that 15 of the seized firearms originated in the United States. Several firearms recovered through the project are prohibited in Canada. Forensic analysis also linked the seized firearms to 14 shootings across the GTA.

items.title: Smaller upgrades, then major renovations to come at Celebration Square in Mississauga
items.summary: Construction will soon begin at Celebration Square in Mississauga’s downtown core, but it’s not the start of the major overhaul that’s eventually planned for the popular outdoor venue. The work scheduled for this fall following the seasonal shutdown on Sept. com. The washrooms will be temporarily closed while the work is completed and are expected to reopen in mid-November. Meanwhile, the much bigger renovation plans for the nearly five-acre outdoor public gathering place could see work begin toward the end of 2027, the city said earlier. What began in 2025 as a plan to make some major improvements to Celebration Square in early 2026 grew into a significantly larger renovation and renewal project that will see big changes to the popular entertainment venue in the next couple of years. com called for the huge square to be outfitted with bigger and better high-resolution viewing screens and new artificial turf. Work was to take place early in 2026 and involve the closing down to the public of the turf lawn area and surrounding pavement for four to six weeks while the existing artificial turf was replaced.

items.title: B.C. man arrested at Mississauga First Nation traffic stop
items.summary: The East Algoma detachment of the Ontario Provincial Police responded to a traffic complaint involving a vehicle that had been reported earlier in Sault Ste. Marie area. On Saturday, Sept. 12, police received a second complaint regarding the same vehicle travelling eastbound on Highway 17 near Iron Bridge. The caller advised that the vehicle was failing to remain within its marked lane. Officers subsequently located the vehicle a short time later on Highway 17 in Mississauga First Nation. During the interaction, police observed signs consistent with impairment by alcohol. items.title: Traferox Technologies Inc. Receives FDA Clearance for the X°Port Heart Preservation System
items.summary: This content may have been approved or produced by a partner MISSISSAUGA, Ontario, Sept. 22, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) — Traferox Technologies, Inc. today announced that the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has granted 510(k) clearance for the X°Port® Heart Preservation System, a device that enables static 10°C heart preservation during transport prior to transplantation. MISSISSAUGA, Ontario, Sept. 22, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) — Traferox Technologies, Inc. today announced that the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has granted 510(k) clearance for the X°Port® Heart Preservation System, a device that enables static 10°C heart preservation during transport prior to transplantation. “The FDA clearance of X°Port Heart marks an important milestone for Traferox and for the continued advancement of 10°C organ preservation,” said Rick Mangat, Chief Executive Officer of Traferox. “The strong clinical evidence supporting 10°C heart preservation, together with the successful adoption of 10°C preservation across leading lung transplant programs, has demonstrated the potential of this approach to improve donor organ preservation and transport. We look forward to working with transplant centers across the US to support the continued adoption of 10°C preservation in routine clinical practice”. The clearance comes as clinical evidence supporting 10°C heart preservation continues to grow. Published, peer-reviewed evidence has linked 10°C heart preservation to improved early outcomes, including reductions in severe primary graft dysfunction and improved post-transplant survival compared to conventional ice storage1 and other hypothermic temperatures2, including in transplants involving higher-risk donor hearts. Vanderbilt University Medical Center was the first US institution to investigate 10°C heart preservation clinically, building on the success of 10°C preservation in lung transplantation.

items.title: Mississauga honours the National Day for Truth and Reconciliation on September 30
items.summary: This day honours the Indigenous children who never returned home, the Survivors of residential schools, and the families and communities whose lives continue to be affected by this legacy. On Wednesday, September 30, the City of Mississauga will once again recognize the National Day for Truth and Reconciliation, and Orange Shirt Day. This day honours the Indigenous children who never returned home, the Survivors of residential schools, and the families and communities whose lives continue to be affected by this legacy. As communities across Canada reflect on the lasting impacts of residential schools, the City remains committed to advancing Reconciliation, increasing awareness and understanding within the community. In the lead-up to September 30, the City will offer a range of educational initiatives and opportunities for learning, reflection and engagement. Community members are encouraged to participate and deepen their understanding of the truth of Canada’s residential school system and the ongoing journey towards Reconciliation. City offices will be closed on Wednesday, September 30 to observe the National Day for Truth and Reconciliation. Regular hours will resume on Thursday, October 1. For more information on what’s open and closed, visit the City’s website. ca 905-615-3200, ext.

items.title: Hospitalization Count from Mississauga Apartment Fire Climbs to 18, CBC Reports
items.summary: CBC Toronto reports that the number of people hospitalized after Monday's fire at a Mississauga apartment building near Inverhouse Drive and Lakeshore Road West has climbed to at least 18, including a firefighter and a Peel police officer. According to CBC, residents of the building were left shaken by the blaze, which broke out in a hallway and forced an evacuation. Peel Regional Police say the fire may have been arson, though investigators had not confirmed a cause as of Monday. The higher count marks an increase from earlier same-day estimates that had put the number of people treated closer to 10 or 11, suggesting more people were assessed for smoke inhalation and other injuries as the day went on. The officer and firefighter who were hurt were both injured while helping other residents get safely out of the building.

items.title: Councillors Call E-Scooters a Safety 'Crisis' as Mississauga Lobbies Queen's Park for Tighter Rules
items.summary: According to INsauga, Mississauga officials have escalated their push for the provincial government to tighten regulations on e-scooters, with one city councillor describing the current situation around the motorized devices as a public safety crisis. Mayor Carolyn Parrish said she expects Ontario's transportation minister, Prabmeet Sarkaria, may soon announce that police across the province will get expanded authority to enforce road rules against e-scooter riders. The provincial government is expected to address e-scooters and e-bikes more broadly, with new regulations anticipated sometime this fall. Parrish and Ward 3 Councillor Chris Fonseca were part of a Mississauga delegation that raised e-scooter safety directly with provincial officials last month at the Association of Municipalities of Ontario conference in Ottawa. The city followed up after that conference with letters to the province spelling out its concerns and requests on several fronts. Parrish told council last Wednesday that the Ottawa trip was really productive and that provincial ministers and other officials listened to the city on several fronts, including on e-scooter safety.

items.title: Sixth Annual Gathering and Healing Weekend Brings Indigenous Art and Ceremony Back to Mississauga
items.summary: According to organizer Eagle Spirits of the Great Waters, the sixth annual Gathering and Healing Weekend and Art Mashkiki Indigenous Art Exhibit returns to the Small Arms Inspection Building in Mississauga from September 25 to 27. The free, public event is open to people of all ages and includes dance, music, storytelling, art, an Indigenous market, food and ceremony meant to share First Nations, Metis and Inuit arts and cultures. Eagle Spirits of the Great Waters is a Mississauga-based, Indigenous-led non-profit that runs the annual weekend in connection with the National Day for Truth and Reconciliation, observed each year on September 30 alongside Orange Shirt Day. Both days are dedicated to honouring Residential School survivors, their families and communities, and to recognizing the lasting impact of Canada's residential school system. The organization says the weekend creates a space for Indigenous and non-Indigenous people to come together through culture, art, learning, remembrance and healing. Opening night on Friday features Indigenous artists and vendors, light refreshments, welcoming remarks, drumming from Eagle Spirits, and live music from Dwayne Laforme and the Boogie Blues Band.
